literal: Those-who-possess before, those-who-do-not-have like, even-having-humbled-oneself those-who-learned; the-lowest-indeed those-who-learned-not.
translation: The learned acquire knowledge by humbling themselves, just as the destitute stand before the wealthy. Those who do not learn are the lowest of all.
modern: செல்வர்கள் முன் ஏழைகள் பணிந்து நிற்பது போல, ஆசிரியரிடம் பணிந்து கற்பவர்களே உயர்ந்தவர்கள். அவ்வாறு கற்காதவர்கள் மிகவும் தாழ்ந்தவர்கள் ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the learned with the unlearned using a powerful social comparison. It compares a student seeking knowledge to a poor person standing humbly before a wealthy person. Those who are willing to humble themselves and yearn for knowledge become the learned and attain greatness. In contrast, those who refuse to humble themselves and remain unlearned are considered the lowest of people.
